purpose: Start productization by converting evidence-backed architecture choices into controlled product requirements while leaving propulsion-current, energy, thermal and mechanical values open where evidence is still insufficient.

change_control.rule: Any change to a FROZEN decision in this file requires a new PRODUCT_BASELINE_PB-xx revision or an explicitly linked engineering change record. Do not silently edit a frozen decision into a different value.

frozen_decisions.rationale: User product target; already the sole previously closed numerical G1 row.

For the 70-100 kg payload class, the eight-propulsor branch materially lowers per-axis thrust/electrical stress versus quad/hex at the upper MTOW screening region and provides a practical degraded-control path. Coaxial packaging keeps the concept compact; coaxial interaction losses remain a sizing input, not ignored.

Product safety baseline: one complete propulsion-channel loss shall not cause an intentional continued mission. Continued hover at maximum payload is not required; sufficient controllability for controlled landing is required and must later be physically proven.
Defines the U1 high-voltage input domain and supports current heavy-lift 18S-class propulsion without forcing an exact cell chemistry or series count yet.

U1 protection, DC-link and layout shall control repetitive semiconductor terminal stress to at most 120 V. Normal operation shall not rely on MOSFET avalanche as the repetitive energy-management mechanism.
frozen_decisions.verification: Measure VDS at the MOSFET terminals during staged switching, regenerative and disconnect tests; no production claim before physical verification.

frozen_decisions.rationale: With an 80 V operating ceiling and a 120 V repetitive transient design ceiling, a 150 V class keeps a controlled voltage margin. The 120 V class would consume the full device rating at the transient ceiling. The efficiency penalty versus current 120 V candidates is accepted at architecture level and will be managed by exact device/parallel-count/thermal optimization.

The legacy DRV8353 100 V-class integrated driver domain is not retained for the 150 V U1 power-stage baseline. Exact high-voltage driver MPN remains open until gate-charge/current, negative switch-node transient and fault-path checks close.

CAN-FD capability provides payload for diagnostics/telemetry while preserving Classic CAN interoperability. Bit rate, upper-layer message map and termination remain separate open implementation values.
Switching permission is deliberately separated from driver awake state; a reset/fault cannot silently resume PWM.
This is the preserved core architecture from the prior program and remains appropriate for the heavy-lift propulsion objective; current/voltage/component values are requalified separately.

still_open_after_pb01: battery mass and exact chemistry/series count
coaxial aerodynamic interference factor and exact arm geometry
hover and peak thrust per rotor
motor/propeller exact MPN and operating point
MOSFET exact MPN and parallel count
anti_hallucination_rule: PB-01 freezes only the listed decisions. A frozen architecture requirement is not a claim that thermal, EMI, dyno, fault-tolerance or flight performance has already been physically verified.
